THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The State has preferred this appeal against the judgment of acquittal passed by the V Addl. District and Sessions Judge, D.K. Mangaluru, sitting at Puttur, D.K., in Crl.A.No.308/2013 dated 20.02.2016.

entities.text: V Addl. District and Sessions Judge, D.K. Mangaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The rank of the parties in this appeal are referred in the same rank as referred by the trial Court.

3. Brief facts of the prosecution case are that:
NC: 2023:KHC:46030 While CW.1/PW.3 was in station, he got credible information as to the accused persons had illegal possession of wild animal articles.

Immediately,
he along with his staff had conducted the raid on 27.09.2005 at about 12.30 p.m. in Bilinele Village, near bus stop of Kaikamaba in Puttur Taluk, where accused Nos.1 to 5 were found with the skin of a panther worth Rs.1,00,000/- for the purpose of sale without licence or permission by means of illegal trespass into the government forest and by killing the panther by hunting for wrongful gain.
Thus, accused have committed the offences punishable under Sections 9, 27, 31, 33, 39, 48A, 50, 51 of Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 (for short 'the Act, 1972') and Section 34 of IPC.

sentences.text: After taking cognizance, a case was registered in C.C.No.2401/2006.
The trial Court framed the chares for the alleged commission of offences.
Charges were read over and explained to the accused.
Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

To prove the case of prosecution, ten witnesses were examined as PWs.1 to 10, marked 12 documents as Exs.P1 to P12, portion of Ex.P4 is marked as Ex.C1 and two materials objects were identified as M.Os.1 and 2.
On closure of prosecution evidence, statement of accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded.
Accused had totally denied the evidence appeared against them, but they did not choose to lead any defence evidence on their behalf.

Portion of statement of PW.9 was marked as Ex.D1.
6.

Sri .M.R.Patil, learned High Court Government Pleader for the appellant/State has submitted his arguments that the impugned judgment and order of acquittal recorded by the learned Sessions Judge is contrary to facts of the case and evidence on record and the same is liable to be set aside.
The reasons assigned by the learned Sessions Judge are erroneous.
The Sessions Judge has reached to a wrong conclusion resulting in substantial miscarriage of justice.
The NC: 2023:KHC:46030 Appellate Court has failed to appreciate the Karnataka State Government orders dated 16.10.1973 and 26.08.2010.
It is very clear from the said order that, the amendment states that, the officer not below the rank of Sub-Inspector of Police is eligible to investigate and submit the charge sheet.
These well settled principles and provisions have been ignored by the Appellate Court which has resulted in acquittal.
Further, it is submitted that there is an apparent error committed by the Appellate Court while dealing with this appeal.
The Appellate Court misconstrued and misread the provisions of Wild Life Protection Act and the Government orders.
The Appellate Court has not properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and on all these grounds, he sought to allow this appeal.

To buttress his submission he relied on the judgment of this court in the case of R.Shivakumar Vs. The State of Karnataka rendered in Crl. Appeal No.1175/2010 and connected appeal decided on 13th July 2018.

8. Having heard the arguments on both sides, the following points would arise for my consideration:
1.
Whether the State has made out a ground to interfere with the impugned judgment of acquittal?
2. What order?

Regarding point No.1:
 NC: 2023:KHC:46030 10.
I have carefully examined the materials placed before this Court.

In paragraphs 16 to 21, the Appellate Court has observed as under:
" 16.
In view of the arguments advanced by learned counsel for appellants it is just and necessary to reproduce Sec.55 of Wild Life Protection Act 1972 which provides as follows 55.

Cognizable offences-No Court shall take cognizance of any offence against this Act except on the complaint of any person other than - (a) the Director of Wild Life Preservation or any other office authorized in this behalf by the Central Government; or (aa) The Member Secretary, Central Zoo Authority in matters relating to violation of provisions of Chapter IVA; or (ab) Member Secretary,
Tiger Conservation Authority or (ac) Director of the concerned Tiger Reserve; or (b) The Chief Wild Life Warden or any other officer authorized in this behalf by the State Government (subject to such conditions as may be specified by that Government); or (bb) The officer in charge of the Zoo in respect of violation of provisions of Sec.38 J; or (c) Any person who has given notice of not less than 60 days, in the manner prescribed, of the alleged offence and of his intention to make a complaint to the Central Government or the State Government or the officer authorized as aforesaid NC: 2023:KHC:46030 17.
As could be seen as rightly argued by learned counsel for appellants CW1 is not authorized person to lodge complaint nor he lodged complaint in accordance with law.
So also Magistrate cannot take cognizance of the offence except on the complaint filed by the person enumerated in Sec.55.

Appeal No.2313/2016 dated 29-05-2012 in the case of State by Rural Police Chinthamani Vs Ramakrishna Reddy and Others.

entities.text: State by Rural Police Chinthamani Vs Ramakrishna Reddy and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In para no.11 and 12 of the said decision it is held that 11.

Therefore, it is seen to initiate action or for the purpose of investigation, complaint has to be submitted to the Magistrate by anyone of the category of persons referred to in Section 55 and upon receipt of such a Complaint, the Magistrate shall take cognizance following the procedure prescribed by Section 200 of the Cr.P.C.
There shall be no doubt on this point it excludes police report or report of the investigation by the police suo moto or on the basis of report submitted to it under Section 154 of the Cr.P.C.

In other words, the SHO of the jurisdictional police shall have no power to investigate commission of offence under the Act except on the basis of the complaint submitted to the Magistrate and referred to him for Investigation.

NC: 2023:KHC:46030 12. Section 55 clarifies that Court shall not take cognizance except on the basis of the complaint submitted by any one of the officers named in Section 55 it excludes final report submitted by the police officials under Section 173 of the Cr.P.C.
19.
The facts and circumstances and principles of above decision are aptly applicable to the present case on hand and they are followed.

In similar situation the Hon'ble High Court of Gujarath at Ahamadabad in Cr.MA/9138/2009 dated 09-05-2012 in the case of Ashok Bhanwarlal Doshi Vs State of Gujarath, which was filed for quashing FIR in Cr.No.2/2005 of Kavda PS registered for the offences under Sec.420, 379 and 120B of IPC and Sec.29 and 51(1) of Wild Life Protection Act 1972 observed that a complaint is required to be lodged by the authorized officer before the concerned Court and it is on a complaint of such officer the court can take cognizance of the offence and therefore allowed the petition and pleased to quash and set aside the FIR registered in Kavda PS Cr.No.2/2005 and the charge sheet filed pursuant thereto, which has been registered as CC 3767 of 2008.

20. In view of the above decisions and the facts and circumstances of the present case on hand, there is much force in the arguments of learned counsel for appellants.
But there is no force in the argument of learned P.P.

The decision relied upon by learned P.P. will not come to the help of prosecution, as facts and - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:46030 circumstances are entirely different from the facts and circumstances of the present case on hand.
21.
In view of the above discussions, it is very much clear that the complaint lodged by PW3 is not in accordance with law and also charge sheet filed by PW8 is also not in accordance with law.

11. On re-examination/reconsideration and re- appreciation of the entire evidence on record, I do not find any illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment of acquittal passed by the Appellate Court.
Hence, I answer point No.1 in negative.

Regarding point No.2:
12.

ORDER 1.

The appeal is dismissed;
